variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) is a managed buffer between a producer that creates work and a consumer that performs it. A producer sends a message and can finish its request without waiting for the consumer. SQS stores the message until a consumer receives it, completes the work, and explicitly deletes the receipt.
variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Choose Standard or FIFO from the business invariant”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Standard queue
pairs.detail: Standard queues provide at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering.
pairs.explanation: Standard queues provide at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering. Choose one when messages can run independently, duplicates are safe, and horizontal throughput matters more than sequence.

pairs.label: FIFO queue
pairs.detail: FIFO queues preserve order within each MessageGroupId and suppress duplicate sends through deduplication IDs.
pairs.explanation: FIFO queues preserve order within each MessageGroupId and suppress duplicate sends through deduplication IDs. Different groups can run concurrently; one hot or blocked group remains serial.

variants.hint: Give each part the one job only it can do, then rule out the rest. The core invariant is receive does not mean complete.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Standard queue: Standard queues provide at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering. FIFO queue: FIFO queues preserve order within each MessageGroupId and suppress duplicate sends through deduplication IDs.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Treat visibility as a renewable processing lease”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Long-poll a bounded batch
pairs.detail: Wait for available work instead of continuously issuing empty receives.
pairs.explanation: Wait for available work instead of continuously issuing empty receives. Keep each batch small enough that every message can finish before its processing lease expires.

pairs.label: Validate before side effects
pairs.detail: Reject malformed, unauthorized, or unsupported versions deliberately.
pairs.explanation: Reject malformed, unauthorized, or unsupported versions deliberately. Permanent contract errors should not consume an unlimited transient-retry budget.

pairs.label: Apply with an operation key
pairs.detail: Write the idempotency key and business effect atomically at the destination.
pairs.explanation: Write the idempotency key and business effect atomically at the destination. A repeated delivery should return the first result or become a no-op.

pairs.label: Extend only live work
pairs.detail: Use ChangeMessageVisibility for legitimate long-running work.
pairs.explanation: Use ChangeMessageVisibility for legitimate long-running work. Stop extending when the worker loses ownership or cannot prove progress.

pairs.label: Delete the current receipt
pairs.explanation: Delete after success. Batch deletes can reduce request pressure, but every entry in a batch can fail independently and must be checked.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Quarantine poison messages without hiding incidents”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Classify the failure
pairs.detail: Retry timeouts, throttling, and brief dependency outages with backoff and jitter.
pairs.explanation: Retry timeouts, throttling, and brief dependency outages with backoff and jitter. Quarantine invalid schemas, missing required identity, and deterministic business-rule failures unless a code or data change can repair them.

pairs.label: Preserve evidence
pairs.detail: Keep the original body, attributes, operation ID, receive count, exception category, and consumer version.
pairs.explanation: Keep the original body, attributes, operation ID, receive count, exception category, and consumer version. Protect sensitive payloads with the same or stronger access and retention controls as the source queue.

pairs.label: Redrive deliberately
pairs.detail: Fix the cause, test representative messages, choose a bounded redrive rate, and watch the destination's capacity.
pairs.explanation: Fix the cause, test representative messages, choose a bounded redrive rate, and watch the destination's capacity. Redriven FIFO work can interleave with newly produced messages.

variants.prompt: From the lesson section “Know when SQS is not the right primitive”: match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Use SQS
pairs.detail: Choose SQS for background jobs, burst absorption, decoupled service commands, and bounded retries where one consumer should complete each message.
pairs.explanation: Choose SQS for background jobs, burst absorption, decoupled service commands, and bounded retries where one consumer should complete each message.

pairs.label: Use SNS or EventBridge
pairs.detail: Use a publisher-and-subscriber service when several independent applications each need their own delivery.
pairs.explanation: Use a publisher-and-subscriber service when several independent applications each need their own delivery. Fan out to separate SQS queues when each subscriber needs buffering and retry isolation.

pairs.label: Use a stream or database
pairs.detail: Use a retained stream when independent consumers must replay history.
pairs.explanation: Use a retained stream when independent consumers must replay history. Use a database when the primary need is transactions, mutable state, or ad hoc queries rather than asynchronous ownership transfer.
